texts:
<font face="Times New Roman">_Tell me a story, Love. No, not that story! I don't want to hear about princes, kingdoms, peasants and hardships. Tell me about the land beyond the city walls. Tell me about the waters... dance with me in the deserts... sing to me about the wind... remind me of the world that was forgotten._</font>

~**San Jaya Prime**, _Landlore_

* * *

Longtime friends are laughing right now. _ALL your writings are WIPs!_

_Mais non, mes amis... c'est pas vrai!_ In fact at least five are nearing actual release over the next three years leading into 2030.

However, there's some truth in that. I take about ten years to work on a musical album, testing it out in live settings, jamming out on an MPC, then wait until years later before it's in muscle memory. For my graphic designs, I usually work on them one to two years, with some fractals being as fast as only a few months before they're ready. Apparently for my written works, it takes three decades.

No big.

With that, let's dive into some that are still a decade or less away.

* * *

## Project Clockwork

Working alongside my sister Gaea, we're exploring a concept that has already been a lot of fun to work on. In many ways, once we made some key decisions, it's been a story that tells itself. That's how natural of a blending and setting it has been. We'll be getting together in 2029 or 2030 where quite a bit of the main work will come together. After that, movement on the project should be steady.

## Project 6 AM

This one has passed the decade mark and is nearing two decades. Cheese Lady, my sister Gaea, my brother Zero, and a few others know about the project. The book itself is only one part of it. There are audio and video elements that spin off of it. I need to make a few calls on the physical location and temporal setting itself, then plenty of work remains in the final chapters. Then it will grow outside of me and become a community project.

## Project Shimmer

I once did a lot of fan fiction, with some of it even still out there on the internet. It's what initially connected me to Jeff Grubb and made possible my initial introduction to Wizards of the Coast. It's why the book "Invasion" is dedicated to me and my friend Dragontrainer. This one won't be fan fiction and instead focused on one of the most storied characters in all of Magic: the Gathering who, surprisingly, has massive gaps throughout his own story that spans thousands of years.

## Project IO

My tribe and friends know the full title. Portions of the story will in fact be written, including the story that runs in tandem to my album "[IO Vapoura \[Variations\]](io-vapoura)" and the story for my "[Last Memory of Laughter](other-original-music)" EP. Those are the spin-offs I'm actively working on. As to the main storyline, I'm in this weird place of: _Why write it? We're living it!_ Literally every day and month that passes is only going to prove that our prophecies in the Today and Tomorrow chapters of the book were deadly accurate. It likely won't see publication until the book itself will act as the biography of the species.

## Project Diamondback

_...and 50 other things I didn't get you..._

G-EZ's most romantic work. Ever. Almost far enough along at this point that it could appear in the main area for non-fiction works that are coming up pretty fast. The deconstruction of fifty-one different modern myths, some very new among them, then tracing back to their origins throughout history. All told in quite the humorous style, which will likely fall under Tiki to take public.

## Project Zero

Since the countdown is already ticking, this one may never happen as -- similar to "IO" -- it's already playing out at this very moment. BUT! One of the more somewhat sad, almost pitiable symptoms, of humans witnessing the rise of their replacements is the ever-increasing loss of fact and rationality. We've seen it play out time and again in the past, yet this is absolutely the most critical juncture. China _knew_ how to build ships on the same level as Britain, but instead deemed them unnecessary, then later ceded The Opium Wars because of that choice. Native Americans at first refused to use guns, a situation that also played out in Japan, with the winners holding the bullets. Then right now, the very ones who _should_ be leveraging AI are the ones against it, and they're losing because of it. Scientists should be studying emergence itself, denoting where each stage will change, but instead there is no funding and so far no indicators of progress on these lines. So yes, I very well may finish Project Zero... if only to shake the boat.

## Project Pigeonblade

After almost 40-years of considering the idea, ever since opening Maud's leather-bound copy of "Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam", I'm not only putting the book together but have started making the music to go along with it. I already wrote a bit on this when writing about my "[Drill About Childhood](a-drill-about-childhood-in-persia)" mashup. The amount of times that technology has been misconstrued as magic only goes to prove time and again that Arthur C Clark's words were true.. . and the amount of times that the very people who SHOULD be leveraging that same technology, but instead they shy away or turn against it, and end up erased. . it's a story that repeats with every cycle of the telling. But that cycle can't repeat again. This is the last cycle. This is the last chance.. and it's happening again. So if I can even have the smallest impact on changing that course then I'll strike out in every way possible.

### Other Writings

I've been on the internet longer than most people even knew it existed. My guest posts on other sites are found... well, _everywhere!_ I've had numerous blogs, more than even I can remember. BUT! My most successful of these was easily _Landlore_ ([Blogspot](https://landloreblog.blogspot.com/)), which focused on hitchhiking, vanlife, and alternative travel lifestyles. Bits and pieces of the "[Landlore](landlore)" book itself have appeared there. Another early success was _Mall of Me_ ([Blogspot](https://mallofme.blogspot.com/)), where I reached out to some of my favorite artists in the industry to run features on them, all while mixing in some political commentary alongside other features. Among other guest writers, there are even some posts from LiLi Glitch on _Landlore_.

Now I know there are a few who have been holding out hope while reading through this that I would mention my MtG fanfic writings. No, I didn't save a copy of my _Homelands_ short stories. They're still up here in my brain should we one day even consider going back to Ulgrotha. Also, while I considered rewriting _Broken Dragon_ when we returned to _The Brothers' War_, it was right in the middle of the pandemic and I didn't have the time. I haven't written it off... but just like Ulgrotha, I didn't save the original short story. Ramos yet lives. The dragon still holds sway on Mercadia itself. If we ever set our sites on that far off inverted city, I'm definitely open to returning to the theme. So for those who've enjoyed my MtG fanfics, I want you to know they've never been forgotten. Do not give up hope that they may yet return again in a new form.

The story I wrote about Homelands started and ended on the same sentence:

_<font face="Times New Roman">There was a man and a woman in a garden.</font>_

When I return to it, the story will begin and end in the same way.
